lines.text: An island of sugar and rum, of rebellion and freedom, that grew into an independent republic. This is the story of Barbados.
English settlers founded Bridgetown in 1628. Its historic centre and garrison are now a World Heritage Site.
Sugar brought rum, and Mount Gay, with a deed from 1703, is among the oldest rum makers in the world.
The sugar was grown by enslaved Africans. In 1816 they rose in Bussa's rebellion, the largest revolt in the island's history.
Errol Barrow, born in 1920, would become the first prime minister and lead Barbados to independence.
Garfield Sobers, born in 1936, became by many reckonings the greatest all-rounder cricket has ever known.
Sandra Mason, born in 1949, would become the first president of the republic.
Mia Mottley, born in 1965, became prime minister in 2018, and led the island to become a republic.
After more than three centuries under the British crown, Barbados became an independent country in 1966.
On the thirtieth of November 1966, the new flag was raised. Fifty-five years later, on the same day, Barbados became a republic.
And from Bridgetown came Rihanna, one of the best-selling singers in the world.
From sugar fields to a republic of its own, Barbados has written its own story.
